correctness.rationale: For \(u=(c,s)^{\mathsf T}\), \(v=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(0<\delta<1\), each exact error update is the symmetric matrix \(U\), \(V_0\), or \(V_\delta\) displayed in RESULT.md. Enumerating all four ordered two-update products establishes the displayed exact \(D_2\). The one-step difference is \(\delta^2vv^{\mathsf T}/2\). Its two-step trace is positive and its determinant is exactly \(-c^2s^2\delta^2[1-s^2\delta(\delta+2)-\delta^4]/16\). The quartic transition function increases strictly from zero to a value greater than one, giving the unique transition; the spectral theorem verifies strictness and the equality line for every admissible real parameter. Exact rational arithmetic independently checks 1,729 representative triples and the witness, whereas symbolic algebra proves the continuum statement. The smallest eigenvalue has leading term \(-cs\delta/4\). No larger-dimensional or long-term result is asserted.

value.rationale: The recent primary algorithm introduces a norm-dependent overrelaxation whose proven one-step loss is no better than ordinary uniform projections, yet longer experimental runs motivate understanding cross-step effects. For the smallest genuinely noncommuting instance, an exact quartic phase boundary and strict two-update reversal identify when this local order can reverse, plus when relaxation becomes universally worse. This is a concrete, motivated structural performance diagnostic, not merely a recomputation of known spectral tables or a cosmetic parameter substitution. It supplies the exact witness, equality line and sharp small-distortion advantage while explicitly limiting claims to two updates.
